s1.syndrome_frame: Subacute onset of involuntary movements in an elderly patient with a history of untreated diabetes mellitus
salient_findings: Involuntary movements of the left upper and lower limbs
Slow response and reduced muscle strength in the left limbs
Positive tendon reflexes in the left limbs
High-signal intensity on T1-weighted images in the bilateral basal ganglia on brain MRI
key_facts: Age: 80 years
Female sex
History of untreated type 2 diabetes mellitus
Duration of symptoms: more than 10 days
Involuntary movements are continuous and irregular
Variable amplitude of involuntary movements
Blood glucose level: 8.59 mmol/L
Hemoglobin A1c: 7.43%
Noncontrast CT of the head shows slightly increased density in the bilateral striatal regions
Brain MRI shows high-signal intensity on T1-weighted images in the bilateral basal ganglia

shortlist.label: Hemichorea-Hemiballismus
shortlist.why_kept: Subacute onset of involuntary movements in an elderly patient

shortlist.label: Diabetic Striatopathy
shortlist.why_kept: History of untreated diabetes mellitus and high-signal intensity on T1-weighted images in the bilateral basal ganglia

shortlist.label: Basal Ganglia Encephalitis
shortlist.why_kept: Subacute onset of symptoms and abnormal brain MRI findings

shortlist.label: Huntington's Disease
shortlist.why_kept: Involuntary movements and basal ganglia abnormalities on imaging

shortlist.label: Wilson's Disease
shortlist.why_kept: Abnormal basal ganglia on imaging and potential for movement disorders

raw.rationale: The patient's history of untreated type 2 diabetes mellitus, combined with the imaging findings of slightly increased density in the bilateral striatal regions on CT and high-signal intensity on T1-weighted images in the bilateral basal ganglia on MRI, are consistent with diabetic striatopathy, which is a rare complication of diabetes.

rejected.label: Hemichorea-Hemiballismus
rejected.why: While the patient presents with involuntary movements, the lack of other characteristic features such as sudden onset and severe chorea makes this diagnosis less likely.

rejected.label: Basal Ganglia Encephalitis
rejected.why: There is no mention of inflammatory markers or other signs of infection, making this diagnosis less likely.

rejected.label: Huntington's Disease
rejected.why: The patient's age and lack of family history or other characteristic features such as cognitive decline and psychiatric symptoms make this diagnosis less likely.

rejected.label: Wilson's Disease
rejected.why: The patient's age and lack of other characteristic features such as Kayser-Fleischer rings, liver disease, or psychiatric symptoms make this diagnosis less likely.
